reviews.summary: WP1 fails because a sweep can miss two solid spheres moving through each other, and several queries give wrong answers on exactly representable geometry. The Mac, Chrome and iPhone simulator reproduced all 12,471 retained vectors bit for bit. Two required fast crossings are missing from those vectors and from the contact-tolerance measurement.

findings.name: Head-on cuboid sweeps return the wrong face normal
findings.different: The clear-ended thin crossings are fixed. Two turned solid cuboids now expose an incorrect head-on face normal.

findings.name: Finite rays miss solid surfaces at their endpoint
findings.different: The prior triangle predicates and missing triangle cases are fixed. Rays ending exactly on a sphere, capsule or cuboid return a false miss.

findings.name: Swapping a point and a turned cuboid changes exact vertex overlap
findings.different: The collinear triangle now agrees in both orders. This case involves a full-dimensional turned cuboid and a point at its exact vertex.

findings.name: Half-gap sweeps accept motion longer than 4,096 units
findings.different: Shape extent validation now rejects the oversize sphere. The separate guard on motion length rounds an overlimit value down to 4,096.

reviews.summary: WP1 fails four of eleven items. Two turned cuboids meeting face to face return a contact normal almost perpendicular to the expected normal, finite rays miss solid surfaces at their endpoints, swapping a point and a cuboid changes exact overlap, and an overlength half-gap sweep passes validation. All ten previous findings are resolved, and all four runtime builds reproduced the 13,288 retained answers.

findings.name: An exactly tangent ray misses a sphere
findings.different: The prior endpoint contacts now hit. This ray misses a sphere at an interior tangency at fraction one half.

findings.name: Head-on cuboid sweeps return the wrong face normal
Finite rays report hits beyond their endpoint
findings.different: The earlier false misses on exact endpoints are fixed. A positive representable clearance is lost when changing frames, causing a false hit beyond the closed segment.

findings.name: Exactly tangent spheres report positive distance from a triangle or capsule
findings.different: The earlier cuboid vertex is correct in both orders. A rounded closest-feature distance rejects an exact tangency in both orders for a sphere against a triangle or capsule.

reviews.summary: WP1 fails three of eleven items. A grazing ray misses a sphere at an exact contact, short rays hit beyond their endpoints, two tangent shape pairs report no overlap, and a cuboid swept head-on into a triangle returns the wrong face normal. The Mac, Chrome and iPhone simulator agree bit for bit on all 13,936 retained answers.

SIM-3D WP1 has failed three reviews in a row on items WP1.2, WP1.3 and WP1.4, each time on new exact-boundary cases the reviewer constructs: an exactly tangent ray missing a sphere, finite rays hitting just beyond or missing at their endpoint, exactly tangent shapes reporting a tiny positive distance, head-on cuboid face normals. Every earlier finding was fixed and the Mac, Chrome and iPhone simulator agree bit for bit, so the builder is converging only case by case. The design's contract (DESIGN.md: overlap 'true exactly where the distance is zero'; finite rays include their endpoint; normals within a dot bound) asks binary32 queries for exact answers at exact tangency, which an unbounded set of constructed cases can break. Decide the boundary contract from first principles for a game physics library (as shipped engines do: a stated contact tolerance or slop, closed-interval rules with a tolerance on ray endpoints, or exact predicates only where cheap) and state it so a reviewer can test it with a finite, named set of cases; update the WP1 items to match. Read .orchestrate/evidence/SIM-3D/WP1-review.md and WP1-review-1.md in .claude/worktrees/sim-3d for the cases. Keep determinism across devices as is. Change only what the boundary contract needs.
